work_order.understanding:
QA failed one case, T-35, with BUG-1: four links below the 44px minimum touch target. I reproduced it exactly against a production build of 598cda8 — the same four measurements, to the pixel (/ A "Tabs" 35x24, /settings A "Tabs" 35x24, /sign-in A "Create an account" 129x16, /sign-up A "Sign in" 48x16) — and then fixed it and re-measured to zero undersized controls. So the reported defect is real, small and now understood.

The previous work order's diagnosis was NOT wrong, but it was incomplete in a way that would have produced a third failure, so I am rewriting it rather than patching the patch. v1's root_cause said "not a defect — the repository is empty by design", which was true and correct about the repository, and it went on to describe the plan's own three self-inflicted defects. It was right about all of them. What it did not do is check its own design against the engine it targets: v1 specified globals.css to declare the six spacing tokens as `--space-1: 4px` through `--space-8: 32px`, and listed `px-space-4`, `gap-space-3`, `mt-space-4` and 48 more uses of that family across 18 files. Tailwind v4 does not generate utilities from a `--space-*` theme namespace. `--space-*` is not a spacing namespace in v4; the spacing scale is `--spacing-*`. I confirmed this in isolation with the pinned tailwindcss 4.3.3: a `@theme` block containing `--space-3: 12px` and a markup file using `gap-space-3` emits NOTHING into the utilities layer, while the same block written `--spacing-space-3` emits `.gap-space-3 { gap: var(--spacing-space-3) }`. So all 51 spacing utility uses in this PR compiled to no rule at all. Every padding, margin and gap in the product was silently zero.

That is the real root cause and it is one line of CSS, not three JSX attributes. The consequence is visible in QA's own evidence: the top bar's three controls measured a 0px gap between them, not the `gap-space-3` (12px) the header asks for, and the cross-link sat flush against the submit button at 0px. docs/ui.md:225 states BOTH clauses in one sentence — "Touch targets are at least 44px by 44px, and no control is within 8px of another control's edge". QA's test only measures the first clause, which is why it reported the links and not the spacing. But the spacing is the underlying defect: it is why the links are crowded at all, and a fix that only added min-height to the three link call sites would have satisfied the one assertion QA happened to write while leaving the product with no spacing anywhere and the second clause of the rule still violated. I checked that empirically rather than assuming: with min-height added but the tokens still inert, the cross-link-to-submit-button gap measured 0px.

The second, independent finding is that min-height alone would not have fixed the links even with spacing working, because these are INLINE anchors. `min-height` does not apply to a non-replaced inline box. I verified this in Chromium: an inline `<a>` with `min-height:44px` measures 85x19 — the utility is silently discarded. Copying the siblings' exact `min-h-[44px] leading-[44px]` onto the cross-links, the obvious patch, leaves them 167x19. They need `inline-flex items-center` to become a block-level box the utility can apply to, and `min-w-[44px]` because QA asserts BOTH axes and the brand link is 35px wide. The brand link additionally needed `inline-flex` for the same reason even though it sits in a flex parent. I also tried and rejected `align-middle` on the cross-links: it is not needed once the spacing tokens resolve, and I removed it to keep the diff minimal.

Nothing in the previous order's design was arbitrary here — the token NAMES (`--space-1`, `gap-space-3`) were chosen to match docs/ui.md's spacing table by name rather than by count, which v1 was deliberate about and which is still the right instinct. The error is that the namespace prefix was carried from v3 syntax into v4. The fix keeps every class name in all 18 files exactly as written and changes only the six token declarations to the v4 namespace.
work_order.root_cause:
Two independent causes, and v1 diagnosed neither.

1. THE PRIMARY CAUSE, and the one v1 got wrong by omission: src/app/globals.css declares the six spacing tokens as `--space-1` … `--space-8` inside `@theme`. Tailwind CSS v4 generates no utilities from a `--space-*` theme namespace — the v4 spacing namespace is `--spacing-*`. Verified against the pinned tailwindcss 4.3.3: a `@theme` block with `--space-3: 12px` emits zero rules for `gap-space-3`, `mt-space-4`, `px-space-4` and the rest; the same token written `--spacing-space-3` emits `.gap-space-3 { gap: var(--spacing-space-3); }`. All 51 spacing utility uses across 18 files under src/ compiled to nothing, so every margin, padding and gap in the product was zero. This is why the top bar's controls sit 0px apart and why the auth cross-link touches the submit button — and it is why docs/ui.md:225's second clause ("no control is within 8px of another control's edge") is violated across the app even though QA only tested the first clause.

2. THE REPORTED SYMPTOM, whose obvious fix does not work: the three under-sized links (src/components/ui/top-bar.tsx brand link; src/components/auth-form.tsx:98 and :107 cross-links) are INLINE anchors, and `min-height` does not apply to a non-replaced inline box — Chromium measures an inline `<a>` carrying `min-height:44px` at 85x19, and the siblings' `min-h-[44px] leading-[44px]` at 167x19. They require `inline-flex items-center` to become a box the utility can size, plus `min-w-[44px]` because QA asserts both axes and the brand link is only 35px wide.

The two interact: with the tokens inert, adding min-height to the links still leaves them 0px from the submit button, so fixing only the links satisfies the assertion QA wrote while leaving the rule it derives from broken.
work_order.approach:
Four edits. The first is the whole fix; the other three make the three links actually reach 44px.

**1. src/app/globals.css — the root cause.** Rename the six spacing tokens from `--space-N` to `--spacing-space-N`, keeping every value and keeping the `space` infix. `--spacing-*` is the v4 spacing namespace, and `--spacing-space-3` is what generates the class name `gap-space-3` — the exact class names already written in all 18 files. No JSX changes, no class renames, no second token family: the existing markup starts working. Do NOT also add a parallel `--space-*` block or switch the call sites to bare `gap-3`/`p-4`; the v3 default spacing scale is already emitted by the Tailwind import, so bare numeric utilities would work too, but they would mean editing 51 call sites and losing the token-name-is-the-docs-table-name property v1 was deliberate about. One block, six lines.

**2–4. The three links.** Each gets `inline-flex min-h-[44px] min-w-[44px] items-center` prepended to its existing classes. `inline-flex` is load-bearing and must not be dropped: without it these are inline boxes and min-height is discarded by the engine, which is the trap that makes the naive patch look like it worked. `min-w-[44px]` is load-bearing on the brand link, which is 35px wide and fails QA's width assertion otherwise. Do not add `align-middle` — measured, it is unnecessary once the spacing tokens resolve, and it is not needed for either clause of the rule.

**A test that reproduces the failure.** jsdom computes no layout and returns 0x0 for every element, so no unit test can assert 44px — tests/components/ui.test.tsx must instead assert the MARKUP that produces it: that the brand link and both auth cross-links carry the min-h and min-w utilities and are not bare inline anchors. That is the regression guard for the JSX half and it fails on the pre-fix source. The 44px and 8px assertions themselves are browser-only, which is exactly why AC-12 is written as a browser criterion: it is the only thing that will catch the CSS half, because the CSS half is invisible to every check CI runs.

**Verified before proposing.** I applied this exact four-edit change to 598cda8, built it, and measured in Chromium at the same four URLs QA used: zero undersized controls (was four), every control >=44px on both axes, inter-control gaps 36/12/16px on the auth screens and 12px across the top bar (was 0px), no horizontal overflow at 360px on any of the four screens, one h1 per signed-in screen, sign-up still lands on /, and vitest 81/81, tsc --noEmit and eslint all clean. The gap figures are the designed token values, which is the check that the tokens now resolve.

Deliberately NOT done: no change to any other component's classes. The 15 other files that use spacing utilities need no edit — they are fixed by the token rename alone, which is the point of fixing the cause rather than the symptom. No change to docs/ui.md or any other approved doc (reserved path). No dark mode, no new primitive.

Keep every value byte-identical and keep the `space` infix so the generated class names are exactly the ones already used in src/ (gap-space-3, mt-space-4, px-space-6 and the other 46 uses). validated_work_order.understanding:
The previous order's root cause was RIGHT and it held. QA's own retest says so in the only words that matter: T-11 measures the served stylesheet and finds `.gap-space-3{gap:var(--spacing-space-3)}` and `.sm\:px-space-6{padding-inline:var(--spacing-space-6)}` in it, with the top bar's nav gap at 12px, the form's gap at 12px, the cross-link paragraph's margin-top at 16px and the card's padding at 16px — the designed token values, which is the confirmation that `--spacing-space-N` really is the namespace that generates `gap-space-3`. BUG-1 is fixed: T-6 retested and passed, and every top-bar control on / and /settings is 44x44 or larger. So I am not rewriting a correct diagnosis for the sake of it. What v2 got wrong is the step after the diagnosis.

**v2 scoped itself to the controls QA had named instead of to the rule, and then verified its scope with an instrument that is blind to the one control still broken.** Its evidence says "undersizedTargets() returns an empty list on all four screens" and its approach says "no change to any other component's classes — the 15 other files need no edit". But `undersizedTargets()` excludes sr-only clips, and the skip link is `sr-only` until it takes focus. The predicate could not see the skip link even in principle. A passing run of it therefore said nothing about the fifth control, and v2 read that silence as proof the sweep was complete. It was not; it was the shape of the hole.

The criterion had the identical blind spot, which is why a full review and a full QA round both walked past it. AC-12's `check` says "every visible control", and its `how_to_verify` says to measure "every visible a, button, input, select and textarea, excluding sr-only clips". The skip link is invisible until focus, so AC-12 as written is unfalsifiable for exactly the control that failed — a criterion and its measuring instrument shared one blind spot, and QA, which is given the criteria and deliberately no memory of last time, faithfully followed the instruction to skip it. Its three uncaught sibling checks (T-6, T-7, T-10) all pass. Only T-9, which explicitly presses Tab and measures the focused state, found BUG-2. I am correcting AC-12's how_to_verify to carve the skip link back out of that exclusion, and stating the skip link's requirement as AC-13 in its own right, so it no longer depends on any tester remembering a carve-out. This is a correction to the measuring instruction, not to the rule: the code is what is wrong, and docs/ui.md:225 is exactly what AC-13 now says.

**BUG-3 is included here although QA filed it as not introduced by this PR, and I want to be plain about why.** QA's attribution is correct in the narrow sense and wrong in the one that matters: its counterfactual shows the padding-zero pre-fix build still overflowed (532 against 360), so the last commit did not cause the overflow. But `src/components/ui/top-bar.tsx` is a file this PR introduces — there is no earlier version of the top bar, or of the product, anywhere in the repository. "Not caused by the previous commit" is not "not this PR's". More practically: QA is given no memory of this run, so if I leave it, the next run rediscovers it and this ticket fails again for a defect I already knew about and had measured. That is the loop this stage exists to break. It is a small fix, in a file this PR owns, against the same rule.

I reproduced both against a production build of d365f2c on http://localhost:3000, in headless Chromium, before changing anything, and I re-measured after. Both reproduce to the pixel: skip link 145.52x40 at (8,8) with min-height 0px, brand link 44x44 at (24,8), axis gap dx=0 dy=0; scrollWidth 548 against clientWidth 360 with the 40-character unbroken name on both / and /settings. After the fix: skip link 145.52x44 at (0,0) with min-height 44px and 16px of clearance to the brand link, and scrollWidth === clientWidth === 360 on all four screens with a 79-character unbroken name.
validated_work_order.root_cause:
Two independent causes. Neither is the spacing-token bug the previous order fixed, and neither is what its own evidence claimed it had verified.

1. src/app/layout.tsx gives the skip link horizontal and vertical space padding and no minimum size. Its height is therefore whatever the text needs: line-height 24px + py-space-2 8px above and below = 40px, four short of the 44px that docs/ui.md:225 requires on BOTH axes. This was true before the token fix too — with py-space-2 compiling to no rule at all it measured 24px — so the previous commit moved it from 24 to 40 rather than from broken to fixed, and nobody was looking. The second half of the same clause fails for a separate reason: `focus:absolute focus:left-space-2 focus:top-space-2` pins the focused link at (8,8), and the top-bar brand link is at (24,8) at 44x44, so the two overlap with dx=0 and dy=0 against a required 8px. Adding a min-height alone would have fixed the height and left the overlap, which is why QA's hint — add the same three utilities the other links carry — is not sufficient on its own. The link also has to stop being positioned over the header: `focus:not-sr-only` already resets position to static, so the fix is to stop overriding it and let the link take its place in the flow.

2. src/components/ui/top-bar.tsx puts a user-supplied string of unbounded width into a flex row with no cap. The display name is validated only as 1..80 characters, so a name with no spaces in it — legal, and what a person whose name really is one unbroken word has — lays the row out at 318px on a 360px screen and pushes document scrollWidth to 548. The row also has no way to shrink: the nav is a flex item with `min-width: auto`, so it cannot go below its content's min-content width, which for an unbreakable word is the whole word.
validated_work_order.approach:
Four edits: the skip link joins the flow and gets a real minimum, one unlayered CSS rule gives it the 8px of clearance docs/ui.md:225 asks for, the top bar caps an unbreakable name, and two unit tests guard the classes that produce both. Every number below was measured in Chromium against a production build of this branch, before and after.

**1. src/app/layout.tsx — the skip link.** Add `skip-link` to the class list; add `focus:inline-flex focus:min-h-[44px] focus:min-w-[44px] focus:items-center`; DELETE `focus:absolute`, `focus:left-space-2` and `focus:top-space-2`. Deleting the positioning is the load-bearing half of this edit and the half QA's hint does not cover: `focus:not-sr-only` already carries `position: static`, and `focus:absolute` — which sorts later in the utilities layer — was overriding it back to absolute, which is the only reason the link ever landed on top of the brand link at all. Once it is in flow nothing can overlap it and the separation clause is satisfied geometrically rather than by hoping. `inline-flex` is load-bearing in the usual way from the previous order: min-height does not bind on a non-replaced inline box, and it is what makes `focus:min-h-[44px]` do anything. Measured after: 145.52x44 at (0,0), display inline-flex, position static, computed min-height 44px.

**2. src/app/globals.css — the 8px of clearance.** The focused link is now a block in the flow directly above the header, and the header's own top padding puts the brand link exactly 8px below it. Eight is the threshold, not the requirement, and a fix that lands on it passes one tester and fails the next. Add one unlayered rule:

    .skip-link:focus { margin-bottom: var(--spacing-space-2); }

It has to be a rule in globals.css rather than `focus:mb-space-2` in the class list, and the reason is worth writing down because it is not guessable: Tailwind emits `not-sr-only`'s `margin: 0` in @layer utilities and it sorts utilities by PROPERTY, so every margin utility is written out before it — the margin loses on order, however it is spelled in the class list. Confirmed in this build's stylesheet: `.mt-space-4` is emitted before `.focus\:not-sr-only:focus`, while `.focus\:absolute:focus` and `.focus\:py-space-2:focus` come after it, which is exactly why position and padding win and margin does not. An UNLAYERED rule outranks every layered rule regardless of order, so this one binds. Measured after: dy = 16px at 1280x720 and 18px at 360x640, against the dx=0 dy=0 QA measured. Leave the rest of globals.css alone — the six `--spacing-space-N` tokens and their comment are correct and QA's T-11 confirms they resolve.

**3. src/components/ui/top-bar.tsx — the unbreakable name.** On the display-name link add `max-w-[120px]`; wrap the name in `<span className="truncate">`; add `min-w-0` to the `<nav>`. All three are needed together and none of them alone is enough: the span is what makes the ellipsis actually render (text-overflow does not reliably apply to a flex container's own text, so putting `truncate` on the link itself is not the same thing), the max-width is what makes the item's min-content contribution finite — an unbreakable word's min-content is the whole word, so without a cap the item cannot shrink no matter what min-width says — and `min-w-0` on the nav is what lets the ROW shrink, since a flex item's automatic minimum is its min-content width and no amount of shrinking inside the nav helps while the nav itself refuses to give ground. 120px is chosen against the product's own fixture: "Ada Q Harness" measures 118.19px and "Priya Raman" is shorter, so ordinary names are not truncated at all and AC-8's "the name appears everywhere the user is shown" is untouched for anyone whose name fits. The existing `min-w-[44px]` on the link stays — it is a floor, not a ceiling, and the 44px minimum is on both axes.

approved_work_order.root_cause:
Two independent causes. Neither is the spacing-token bug the previous order fixed, and neither is what its own evidence claimed it had verified.

1. src/app/layout.tsx gives the skip link horizontal and vertical space padding and no minimum size. Its height is therefore whatever the text needs: line-height 24px + py-space-2 8px above and below = 40px, four short of the 44px that docs/ui.md:225 requires on BOTH axes. This was true before the token fix too — with py-space-2 compiling to no rule at all it measured 24px — so the previous commit moved it from 24 to 40 rather than from broken to fixed, and nobody was looking. The second half of the same clause fails for a separate reason: `focus:absolute focus:left-space-2 focus:top-space-2` pins the focused link at (8,8), and the top-bar brand link is at (24,8) at 44x44, so the two overlap with dx=0 and dy=0 against a required 8px. Adding a min-height alone would have fixed the height and left the overlap, which is why QA's hint — add the same three utilities the other links carry — is not sufficient on its own. The link also has to stop being positioned over the header: `focus:not-sr-only` already resets position to static, so the fix is to stop overriding it and let the link take its place in the flow.

2. src/components/ui/top-bar.tsx puts a user-supplied string of unbounded width into a flex row with no cap. The display name is validated only as 1..80 characters, so a name with no spaces in it — legal, and what a person whose name really is one unbroken word has — lays the row out at 318px on a 360px screen and pushes document scrollWidth to 548. The row also has no way to shrink: the nav is a flex item with `min-width: auto`, so it cannot go below its content's min-content width, which for an unbreakable word is the whole word.
approved_work_order.approach:
Four edits: the skip link joins the flow and gets a real minimum, one unlayered CSS rule gives it the 8px of clearance docs/ui.md:225 asks for, the top bar caps an unbreakable name, and two unit tests guard the classes that produce both. Every number below was measured in Chromium against a production build of this branch, before and after.

**1. src/app/layout.tsx — the skip link.** Add `skip-link` to the class list; add `focus:inline-flex focus:min-h-[44px] focus:min-w-[44px] focus:items-center`; DELETE `focus:absolute`, `focus:left-space-2` and `focus:top-space-2`. Deleting the positioning is the load-bearing half of this edit and the half QA's hint does not cover: `focus:not-sr-only` already carries `position: static`, and `focus:absolute` — which sorts later in the utilities layer — was overriding it back to absolute, which is the only reason the link ever landed on top of the brand link at all. Once it is in flow nothing can overlap it and the separation clause is satisfied geometrically rather than by hoping. `inline-flex` is load-bearing in the usual way from the previous order: min-height does not bind on a non-replaced inline box, and it is what makes `focus:min-h-[44px]` do anything. Measured after: 145.52x44 at (0,0), display inline-flex, position static, computed min-height 44px.

**2. src/app/globals.css — the 8px of clearance.** The focused link is now a block in the flow directly above the header, and the header's own top padding puts the brand link exactly 8px below it. Eight is the threshold, not the requirement, and a fix that lands on it passes one tester and fails the next. Add one unlayered rule:

    .skip-link:focus { margin-bottom: var(--spacing-space-2); }

It has to be a rule in globals.css rather than `focus:mb-space-2` in the class list, and the reason is worth writing down because it is not guessable: Tailwind emits `not-sr-only`'s `margin: 0` in @layer utilities and it sorts utilities by PROPERTY, so every margin utility is written out before it — the margin loses on order, however it is spelled in the class list. Confirmed in this build's stylesheet: `.mt-space-4` is emitted before `.focus\:not-sr-only:focus`, while `.focus\:absolute:focus` and `.focus\:py-space-2:focus` come after it, which is exactly why position and padding win and margin does not. An UNLAYERED rule outranks every layered rule regardless of order, so this one binds. Measured after: dy = 16px at 1280x720 and 18px at 360x640, against the dx=0 dy=0 QA measured. Leave the rest of globals.css alone — the six `--spacing-space-N` tokens and their comment are correct and QA's T-11 confirms they resolve.

**3. src/components/ui/top-bar.tsx — the unbreakable name.** On the display-name link add `max-w-[120px]`; wrap the name in `<span className="truncate">`; add `min-w-0` to the `<nav>`. All three are needed together and none of them alone is enough: the span is what makes the ellipsis actually render (text-overflow does not reliably apply to a flex container's own text, so putting `truncate` on the link itself is not the same thing), the max-width is what makes the item's min-content contribution finite — an unbreakable word's min-content is the whole word, so without a cap the item cannot shrink no matter what min-width says — and `min-w-0` on the nav is what lets the ROW shrink, since a flex item's automatic minimum is its min-content width and no amount of shrinking inside the nav helps while the nav itself refuses to give ground. 120px is chosen against the product's own fixture: "Ada Q Harness" measures 118.19px and "Priya Raman" is shorter, so ordinary names are not truncated at all and AC-8's "the name appears everywhere the user is shown" is untouched for anyone whose name fits. The existing `min-w-[44px]` on the link stays — it is a floor, not a ceiling, and the 44px minimum is on both axes.

**4. tests/components/ui.test.tsx — the two reproductions.** Both fail on the pre-fix source and pass on the fixed one; I checked that by reverting src/ and re-running, and both went red. The skip-link case renders <RootLayout> directly (it is a plain synchronous component with no runtime imports, so testing-library can render it) and asserts the focus:min-h/min-w/items-center/inline-flex utilities are present AND that focus:absolute, focus:left-space-* and focus:top-space-* are gone — the second half is the regression guard for the half that is easy to undo by muscle memory. The top-bar case asserts max-w-[120px] on the name link, truncate on the span inside it, and min-w-0 on the nav. jsdom computes no layout and returns 0x0 for every element, so these assert the CLASSES that produce a 44px target and a bounded width, never a measured size; say so in a comment, because the measured claims are AC-13 and AC-14 and a later reader must not "strengthen" these into getBoundingClientRect assertions that would always return zero.

**Verified end to end before proposing.** I built d365f2c with exactly these four edits and measured in headless Chromium at 1280x720 and 360x640 across all four screens, with the display name set to the 40-character unbroken word and again to a 79-character one. Undersized controls: none, anywhere (was one, the skip link). Pairs within 8px: none, anywhere (was the skip link overlapping the brand link at dx=0 dy=0). scrollWidth vs clientWidth at 360px: 360 === 360 on all four screens, with both the 40- and 79-character names (was 548 vs 360). Sign-up still lands signed in on /, the skip link is still the first tab stop and still activates #main, the top bar still carries Groups and Sign out at full size, and tsc --noEmit, eslint and vitest (86 passed, 7 files) are all green.

Deliberately NOT done: no change to AC-12's `check`, which is correct and which QA's T-6/T-7/T-8/T-10 pass; no change to docs/ui.md or any approved doc; no change to the auth-form cross-links or the brand link, both of which QA re-verified at 44x44 this round; and no lint rule or build-time guard for unresolvable theme namespaces, which is still the right guard and still deliberately a later ticket rather than a fourth edit here.
